description: Push docker images directly to remote servers without an external registry

summary.one_liner: Unregistry is a lightweight container image registry that serves images from the Docker daemon's containerd store, and its `docker pussh` plugin pushes images straight to remote Docker servers over SSH without an external registry.
summary.what_it_does: Unregistry runs as a registry that reads and writes images in containerd's image store, which Docker uses underneath. The included `docker pussh` CLI plugin takes a local image and a user@server target, opens an SSH tunnel, starts a temporary unregistry container on the server, forwards a random local port to it, and runs `docker push` so only missing layers transfer. The image then becomes available to the remote Docker daemon, and the temporary container and tunnel are torn down. Options include a custom SSH port, an identity file, a custom SSH config file, a specific platform for multi-platform images, and a pinned unregistry image version. The README also documents running unregistry standalone as a local registry on port 5000.
use_cases: deploy a locally built image to a production server without a registry
push Docker images to a remote host from CI/CD
transfer only changed layers of an image over SSH
distribute images in air-gapped or isolated networks
run a simple local Docker registry backed by the Docker daemon
avoid paying for or hosting a private container registry
notable: Pushes only missing image layers over an SSH tunnel, with no registry, no public exposure, and no intermediate storage
Uses containerd image store so pushed images are immediately available to Docker without a second pull
Works as a standalone local registry by mounting the containerd socket
Built on Docker Distribution and inspired by Spegel, per the README
Created for the Uncloud multi-host container deployment tool
caveats: Windows is not supported; the README suggests WSL 2 instead
Remote server needs Docker running, SSH access with docker permissions, and internet access to ghcr.io on first use unless the image is preloaded manually
Unregistry container runs as root to access the containerd socket
Without containerd image store enabled, images are stored twice and unmanaged containerd images can fill disk over time; enabling the store can temporarily hide existing classic-store images
